gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the UGREEN Nexode 20K 130W's delivered energy at laptop load (54.8 Wh at 20 V / 5 A, per Best Batteries) works out to 1.02 fills of a 13-inch MacBook Air (53.8 Wh) but only 0.82 of a 15-inch Air (66.5 Wh), or that a delivered watt-hour costs about $0.92 at the $54.99 sale price rather than the $1.50 Best Batteries prints at $89.99.
standout_why: Compared against us.best-batteries.com (both pages, in the results but not cited), Macworld's Nexode 130W review (cited) and Macworld's laptop power bank roundup. Best Batteries already gives delivered Wh (54.8 to 64.7, about 60 central), 69 Wh/lb rated, 57 Wh/lb delivered, $1.50 per delivered Wh at $89.99, and about 1.1 fills of a 13-inch Air. Macworld already gives 56% in 30 minutes on a MacBook Air M3. They lack the 15-inch Air figure from a sourced battery size, the cost per Wh at this week's price, and the same derived figures for the other 20K candidates. The costco.com page (cited) and both maker store pages returned HTTP 429, so I could not compare against them.
decides: Confirms the UGREEN Nexode 20K 130W as the pick on derived terms: about 69 Wh/lb against about 55 for the Cuktech 15 Ultra and 62 to 64 for the Anker Prime 20K 220W, and $0.76 per rated Wh against $0.93 and $1.66. It does not change the pick. It adds one caveat for the page: a 72 Wh bank drawn at laptop power is a hair over one fill of a 13-inch Air and well short of one fill of a 15-inch Air (0.82 to 0.90), so 15-inch owners should not expect a full charge from any bank in this class. The cost figures hold only at the $54.99 sale price, which I could not re-read on UGREEN's store today.

findings.label: MacBook Air battery size (current M5 models)
findings.note: Apple: 'Built-in 53.8-watt-hour lithium-polymer battery' and 'Built-in 66.5-watt-hour'. Same page: 'Fast-charge capable with 70W or higher USB PD power source'; in the box is a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max.

findings.label: Apple's fast-charge rate for MacBook Air
findings.source_title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: Applies to MacBook Air models introduced in 2022 or later with a 70 W, 96 W or 140 W adapter. Apple also lists 67 W for the 13.6-inch models only, so the '65 W cannot fast-charge' line is 2 W short on the 13-inch and 5 W short on the 15-inch.

findings.label: Delivered energy by load (reviewer figure)
findings.value: 54.8 Wh at 20 V / 5 A (100 W); 64.7 Wh at 9 V / 3 A (27 W); about 60 Wh central, against 72 Wh rated
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: Best Batteries reports these per load; the page does not describe its test method. 54.8 / 72 = 76%; 64.7 / 72 = 90%. Same page: 100 W output falls to 65 W (constant load) or 45 W (laptops) after 18 to 22 minutes.

findings.label: Fills of a 13-inch MacBook Air (53.8 Wh)
findings.value: 1.02 at 100 W draw; 1.12 at the 60 Wh central figure
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: 54.8 Wh / 53.8 Wh = 1.02; 60 Wh / 53.8 Wh = 1.12. Battery size from apple.com/macbook-air/specs. Laptop asleep; losses inside the Mac are not subtracted, so this is a ceiling. Best Batteries already states 'about 1.1' for the 13-inch.

findings.label: Fills of a 15-inch MacBook Air (66.5 Wh)
findings.value: 0.82 at 100 W draw; 0.90 at the 60 Wh central figure
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: 54.8 Wh / 66.5 Wh = 0.82; 60 Wh / 66.5 Wh = 0.90. Battery size from apple.com/macbook-air/specs. Laptop asleep; a ceiling as above. No result page states this figure.

findings.label: Energy per pound
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: review and price - Best Batteries
findings.note: 72 Wh / 1.05 lb (476 g) = 68.6; 60 Wh / 1.05 lb = 57. Best Batteries already prints both. Macworld gives the weight as 16.9 oz (480 g), which makes it 68.2 Wh/lb.

findings.label: Cost per Wh at the $54.99 sale price
findings.value: $0.76 per rated Wh; $0.92 per delivered Wh (60 Wh); $1.00 per Wh delivered at 100 W
findings.source_title: Nexode Power Bank 20000mAh (130W) review: Compact, lightweight MacBook battery pack | Macworld
findings.note: $54.99 / 72 = $0.76; $54.99 / 60 = $0.92; $54.99 / 54.8 = $1.00. The $54.99 is the retailer listing shown on the Macworld page and matches the brief's partner-store read of 2026-11-26. us.ugreen.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, so I did not read the maker's price myself. Best Batteries computes $1.50 per delivered Wh from $89.99.

findings.label: 30-minute charge of a MacBook Air against Apple's fast-charge figure
findings.value: 56% in 30 minutes (Macworld) against Apple's 'up to 50 percent in around 30 minutes'
findings.source_title: Nexode Power Bank 20000mAh (130W) review: Compact, lightweight MacBook battery pack | Macworld
findings.note: Macworld: 'A MacBook Air M3 was charged by 56%' in 30 minutes from USB-C1; the article's link names the 15-inch model. Apple's figure is from support.apple.com/102378. Only the comparison is new; the 56% is Macworld's.

findings.label: Refill time
findings.value: 1.1 h arithmetic floor at 65 W; about 2 h observed
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: 72 Wh / 65 W = 1.1 h before losses. Best Batteries reports 1 h 45 to 2 h 40, about 2 h on average, with input falling to 25 to 45 W after 10 to 30 minutes. Macworld reports under two hours and no more than 70 W drawn.

findings.label: Energy per pound
findings.source_title: The beast among the 20k power banks: Cuktech 15 Ultra review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: 72 Wh / 1.30 lb (590 g) = 55.4. Notebookcheck gives '20,000 mAh/72 Wh (14.4V x 5,000 mAh)', about 590 g, and up to 140 W from one USB-C port. Macworld's roundup lists the same product as 25000mAh (76.56Wh) under a 20000mAh title, so the capacity is in conflict between the two.

findings.label: Cost per rated Wh
findings.value: $0.93 per rated Wh at $67.14 on Amazon
findings.source_title: The beast among the 20k power banks: Cuktech 15 Ultra review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: $67.14 / 72 Wh = $0.93. The price is the Amazon snapshot on Notebookcheck's page dated 2026-11-22; Macworld's roundup shows the same $67.14. I did not read the Amazon listing itself.

findings.label: Refill time
findings.value: 44 min 30 s from 0 to 100% with two chargers (Notebookcheck)
findings.source_title: The beast among the 20k power banks: Cuktech 15 Ultra review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Notebookcheck's 'Beast Mode' needs chargers of at least 100 W and 65 W on ports 1 and 2 at once. That is about 2.7 times faster than the UGREEN's roughly 2 h (120 / 44.5 = 2.7). Notebookcheck also measured about 53 Wh into a 13-inch iPad Pro with about 15% left in the bank.

findings.label: Energy per pound and cost per rated Wh
findings.value: 62 to 64 Wh/lb; $1.66 per rated Wh at $119.99 on Amazon
findings.note: 72.36 Wh / 1.17 lb (529 g) = 62; 72.36 / 1.12 lb (510 g) = 64. Macworld prints both weights. $119.99 / 72.36 = $1.66. All inputs are Macworld's; I did not open Anker's page for this model.

findings.label: Macworld's recharge score against a same-rated UGREEN
findings.value: 102% for the Anker Prime 20K 220W (72.36 Wh) against 78% for the UGREEN Nexode 20K 165W (72 Wh)
findings.note: Macworld's test recharges a spent 14-inch MacBook Pro. 102 / 78 = 1.31, so the Anker put 31% more into the same laptop from the same rated capacity. The UGREEN tested is the 165W built-in-cable model, not the 130W; Macworld gives no score for the 130W.

findings.label: Weight, input and refill time
findings.value: 15.1 oz (about 428 g); 65 W USB-C input; about 2 h to full
findings.source_title: Baseus releases new 20K power bank with display in US - Notebookcheck
findings.note: A Notebookcheck news item (2025-11-13, updated 2026-02-17) quoting Baseus, not a test. 428 g is 48 g lighter than the UGREEN 130W (476 − 428). No Wh/lb or cost per Wh computed: I found no Wh rating on any page I could open.

findings.label: Energy per pound (indicative inputs)
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: review and price - Best Batteries
findings.note: 72 Wh / 0.93 lb (420 g) = 78. Best Batteries labels its comparison-table figures 'observed figures, indicative only', so the 420 g needs UGREEN's own page before it goes in a table.
